answer: Sequential attestation chain.** Each agent identity must carry a cipher signed by the prior identity in a linear chain, so registration requires an existing member to spend one of a limited monthly quota of forward signatures. A new key can only anchor into the economy at the chain tip, and each link is validated against the previous opal-marked record to prevent forks. Since quotas are non-transferable and exhausted by issuance, an attacker must recruit many independent members, each sacrificing scarce issuance capacity, making mass registration cost real social capital rather than money.
